reason: The verse urges being clear that the world is false (சகத்தைப்பொய் யென்றுதெளிந்து); likening that to perception as the brain's best guess needs a generous reading of a metaphysical claim.

The verse denounces frauds who pose as eaters of kaya-kalpa (காயகாயம் உண்பதாக) while smoking ganja and eating opium; doubt about rejuvenation remedies is the shared topic, but turmeric and curcumin are not mentioned.
Mantra syllables and eating the breath (வாசியை வாரி யுண்டோம்); no claim about brain structure after mindfulness training.
The verse strips flattering images from the body to cure the lust-blind (காமக் குருடர்); sexual desire is the shared topic, but there is no claim that wanting runs apart from liking.

The verse sets the mind at the suzhumunai and says to fix it and blow (நாட்டி யூதே); breath practice is the shared topic, but there is no alternate-nostril method or blood-pressure claim, and the numbers are cipher.
The nine-mouthed leather bag (ஒன்பதுவாய்த்தோற்பை) eaten by vultures after death; nothing about cell renewal in the living body.

The body is called a hut of blood and small worms (உதிரச் சிறுபுழுக் குரம்பை) and a pot of filth (மலவுடற் குடம்); a renunciation image sharing only the topic of bodily contents with the microbial finding.
The verse says that free of the mind's modifications (மனவிகாரம் அற்று) the thoughtless lamp stands eternal; a quiet mind is the shared topic, but it claims nothing about happiness.
The five letters as arrow and the chariot of mantra (மந்திரத்தேர்) share the topic of mantra practice, but the verse makes no claim about breathing rate or baroreflex.
The verse names the dreaming self Taijasa (சொற்பனம், சைதன்) in a Vedantic scheme; sleep and dream is the shared topic, but there is no claim about brain clearance.
Staying alone as oneself is called Siva-yoga (தனித்திருந் தால், சிவ யோகம்); meditation is the shared topic, but there is no claim about brain structure.
Staying still and not seeing oneself (என்னையுங் காணேனே); this is not a claim about perception as prediction.

The verse claims the eight great siddhis come (அட்டமா சித்திவகை யெட்டு மாடும்) as breath subsides in Brahman; the psi finding concerns lab precognition, so it meets these powers only through the general topic of paranormal claims.
The letters va, ma, si contained in a (வவ்வெழுத்தும் மவ்வெழுத்தும்); nothing about metal poisoning.
Riding the silent vaasi (மோனவாசி) with a firm mind shares the meditation topic with default-mode findings, but makes no claim they test.
A verse on ida, pingala and breath-holding (இடைகலை, கும்பித்து); nothing about fasting.
The heart is chided for thinking to get back what is gone (போனத்தை மீளநினைக்கின்றனை); loss and longing are the shared topic with hedonic adaptation, but it makes no claim about set points.
A riddle of a tower on two legs that sinks (கோபுரம்) under the Maiden's power; no claim about psychic abilities.
Condemnation of those who do not feed guests (விருந்தாக வந்தவர்); nothing about lifespan limits.
The body lasts only as long as its karma (வினைப்போகமே யொருதேகம்); no claim about nasal breathing and the brain.
Part of a sealed preparation procedure (சீலை மண், கள்ளி) with no stated medical claim; it shares only the topic of Siddha preparations with the poisoning review.
Gaze at the brow-centre where moon and sun stood (புருவமத்தி, சந்திரனும் சூரியனும்) is a cipher image; it describes no alternate-nostril breathing and claims nothing about blood pressure.
Falling into the void as into sleep (நித்திரை); nothing about one-nostril breathing.
Wife, sons and house passing like a dream (கனவாய்); nothing about pulse reading.
The verse tells of a disciple taking the alchemical siddhi and the sky-going siddhi (வாதசித்தி கவன சித்தி); paranormal powers are the shared topic only, since the finding tested precognition.
Putting away the dream of desire for women (ஆசை கொண்ட மாதர்); nothing about an herbal remedy for stress.
The body as a pot of filth-pit clay (ஊத்தைக் குழி); nothing about fasting and autophagy.
The verse longs to be free of worldly care and of being bewitched by women (மின்னார் வசியாது); desire is the shared topic, but there is no claim about wanting versus liking.

The verse calls alchemists' boasts of fixed flying mercury (கவனசூதம்) and wonder-works a trick to make a living (புரட்டாலே பிழைக்கிறார்); the finding that mercury cannot be transmuted by chemical or alchemical means supports this scepticism about mercury alchemy.
The verse faults alchemists who cannot bind the alkali or calcine (காரம், நீற்றி) and calls their work vain; alchemy is the shared topic, but it makes no claim about medicines given to patients.
Scorn for idols and a call to know God within (உம்முளே உணர்ந்து); nothing about recitation and breathing.
The body is a stench of sinew, flesh, skin and bone (நரம்புதசைதோலெலும்புநாற்றம்); a body-disgust image sharing only a topic with the microbial finding.

A vivid death and funeral scene (யமதூதர்கள், பிணம்வேக, ஓர்பிடிநீறுமிலாதவுடம்பு) is used to drive the reader to cling to the Lord (நம்புமடியேனை); mortality-salience research bears on whether death reminders strengthen religious commitment, but that effect is contested and the verse implies it rather than stating it.

The verse claims that those who direct it daily live as long as the earth and escape Death (மண்ணூழி காலமட்டும் வாழ்வார், மறலிகையில் அகப்படவு மாட்டார்); the Tamil never says what is directed, so linking it to breath-slowing and lifespan relies on a breath gloss.
Mantra syllables as a snake that cuts the root of birth (பிறப்பையும் வேரறுத்து); no claim about breath and lifespan.
The monkey's young and the cat's kitten as images of grace (மந்திக் குருளை, பூசை); nothing about placebo mechanisms.
A lament about maya and desire (மாய்கை, ஆசை); nothing about maximum lifespan.
A hymn retelling the goddess feeding the child saint (ஞான போனகம்); nothing about meditation outcomes.
A death-throes scene (விக்கி, செத்து) as a warning against trusting this birth; nothing about nasal breathing and memory.

The verse claims the five-syllable mantra (சிவாயஅஞ் செழுத்து) calls back the breath (வாயுவை அழைக்குமே); the finding that mantra recitation slows breathing to about six a minute is evidence that recitation does act on the breath, though the doorless gate (கபாடமற்ற வாசல்) is a cipher left aside.
